name: Battle of Poitiers, Edward the Black Prince
summary: Edward the Black Prince defeats a much larger French army at Maupertuis (near Poitiers) on September 19, 1356. King John II of France is captured along with his son Philip and a large portion of the French nobility. The ransom demanded, 3 million gold écus, is so enormous that France cannot pay it; John eventually returns voluntarily to English captivity and dies in London in 1364. The capture triggers the Jacquerie peasant revolt and the political crisis of the Estates General.

_quarry.structural_significance: The capture of King John II demonstrates that the English military system (longbow archers using terrain and dismounted knights as heavy infantry) could defeat much larger French cavalry armies; the enormous ransom strips France of gold that funds English military campaigns; the political chaos following Poitiers (Jacquerie, Marcel's revolution) shows that the Hundred Years' War is also an internal French constitutional crisis
